findings.finding: Two children regenerate the same generated file docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md with no ordering constraint between them, creating an ordering / implicit-shared-state interaction. Child 0d5f regenerates the guide to reflect the T10 scope-clause edit; child ea28 regenerates it to add the T15 section. The file is fully regenerated from the registry (one section per criterion, do-not-hand-edit), so a correct final guide requires the LAST regeneration to run after BOTH the T10 rubric edit and the T15 registry registration have landed. 0d5f declares no dependency on ea28 (and vice-versa), so nothing sequences the two regenerations.
findings.location: child 0d5f-6745-16bc-403c and child ea28-020e-8215-4eb9 (both write docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md)
findings.suggested_fix: Add a dependency edge (0d5f depends_on ea28) or a single closing regeneration step that runs after both criterion edits, ensuring the last full-file regeneration reflects both T10 and T15.

Child 754c ACs are all about MOVE_REGISTRY["16"], the docs-table mirror, and the author guide — none asserts a comment on the parent epic.

findings.finding: Parent acceptance criterion #4 — 'the coach-move decision (add or reject the proposed out-of-loop-proof move) is recorded on this epic as a comment naming the decision and its rationale' — targets a comment recorded ON THE PARENT EPIC itself. No sibling's acceptance criteria deliver that observable outcome: child 754c-f6bd-0326-4ee8 implements move 16 (embodying the 'add' decision) and records the approval/rationale on its OWN ticket, but its ACs do not produce or assert a decision comment on the parent epic. findings.suggested_fix: Treat AC #4 as a parent-level deliverable: record a comment on the epic naming the add/reject decision for the out-of-loop-proof move and its rationale (cross-referencing 754c's APPROVED decision), rather than relying on any child to produce it.

findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit step/AC (on the epic or on 754c) to post the coach-move decision-and-rationale comment on epic 8fc2, since 754c's current ACs stop at code artifacts.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the T15 Motivation / explain text, name the established prior-art practice it codifies (spike solution / tracer-bullet / walking-skeleton / steel-thread; shift-left / fail-fast) so the criterion is grounded rather than framed as novel.
evidence: Plan Motivation: 'No existing criterion rewards front-loading those checks into a cheap local run or a manual probe against the real target.'

Web prior art retrieved: infrastructure-as-code.com 'Tracer Bullet Pipeline' — 'Build the walking skeleton before fleshing out features. It de-risks the architecture and the deployment pipeline simultaneously'; Pragmatic Programmer tracer-bullet / steel-thread; multiple 'shift-left testing in CI/CD' guides.
The 'prove-then-codify' + 'fastest feedback path' framing is the spike/tracer-bullet + shift-left pattern under a new name.
findings.finding: The plan codifies an established, named SE practice (spike solution / tracer-bullet / walking-skeleton / steel-thread from The Pragmatic Programmer; shift-left / fail-fast) but frames it as novel and cites no prior art, so its authoring (Motivation, explain text) does not ground the criterion in the practice it enforces.
findings.location: Plan section 'Add plan-review criterion T15 ... Motivation' / the T15 rubric design-of-record
scenarios: Reviewers and plan authors reading `rebar explain T15` get no anchor to the decades-old practice, weakening comprehension and adoption.
A future author proposes a near-identical criterion because T15's authoring never named the pattern it embodies.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to the Motivation and the generated T15 guide section noting that T15 operationalizes the tracer-bullet/steel-thread and shift-left de-risking practices at plan-review time, and that its contribution is enforcing prove-then-codify rather than inventing the idea.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a short justification distinguishing T15 from G5's SEQUENCING de-risk clause (and the empirical/feasibility overlays), confirming T15's pre-codification experiment scope is distinct and not repackaging existing de-risk-sequencing judgment.
evidence: G5 guide text: 'SEQUENCING: judge whether a thin vertical-slice / evidence-gated MVP de-risks the riskiest piece first, versus a horizontal big-bang.'
Plan only partitions against T10 ('The de-risk ... phase and T10's production-hardening phase must not overlap') and names no other adjacent criterion.
G5 is conceptually adjacent to T15's 'prove risky mechanisms first' but the plan never distinguishes them.
findings.finding: The plan justifies T15's novelty only against T10 (via the boundary partition) and does not consider G5, whose SEQUENCING clause already rewards de-risking the riskiest piece first — leaving unaddressed whether T15 repackages existing de-risk-sequencing judgment already in the registry.
findings.location: Plan section 'Required companion change: T10 boundary partition' (only neighbor considered)
scenarios: A reviewer questions whether T15 duplicates G5's existing de-risk-sequencing coaching, and the plan offers no differentiation.
Two criteria fire on the same de-risking gap, producing redundant findings.
findings.suggested_fix: Note that G5 judges decomposition/sequencing (which piece to build first) while T15 requires an out-of-loop EXPERIMENT that returns a verdict before codifying into the slow loop — a distinct, per-mechanism empirical proof, not a sequencing choice.
